claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy is an ordered, single-phase hexagonal material.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited transition produces a large but hysteretic entropy change.
The as-deposited material has limited heat-exchange capability because of low surface-to-volume ratio or coarse structural features.
A short post-deposition anneal slightly below the transition temperature followed by rapid quenching will induce nanoscale chemical disorder.
The annealing and quenching treatment will refine the alloy's grains.
The treatment will produce nanoscale regions of incoherent chemical short-range order at grain boundaries that modestly disturb long-range order.
Annealing-induced nanoscale disorder lowers the local elastic-energy barriers governing the magnetostructural transition.
Lower local transformation barriers cause the magnetostructural transformation to become more gradual and spatially distributed.
A more gradual and spatially distributed transformation reduces magnetization and thermal hysteresis.
The annealed alloy will retain a large magnetocaloric entropy change per cycle despite transition broadening.
Grain refinement increases effective heat-exchange area and therefore increases heat-exchange rate.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will display a broader magnetocaloric transition.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will have smaller hysteresis-loop widths in magnetization and thermal measurements.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will exchange heat faster.
The predicted behavior applies during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles near the transition temperature.
The predicted benefits apply only within a processing window that introduces enough disorder to moderate the transition without causing degradation or secondary-phase formation.
The proposed behavior is specific to the stated non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type composition and similar deposition conditions.
